content.text:
h10.

**`(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — ~38 inbound call sites (~36 distinct calling functions)**

### How it breaks down

| Caller file | Sites |
|---|---|
| `internal/filter/functions_test.go` | 17 |
| `internal/filter/engine_test.go` | 8 |
| `internal/filter/time_test.go` | 6 |
| `store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go` | 2 |
| `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go`, `store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go` | 1 each |
| `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go`, `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go` | 1 each |
| `internal/filter/helpers.go` | 1 |

It's the single entry point every SQL dialect backend and API filter-validation path goes through, so it's the top fan-in symbol whether you measure call sites or distinct callers.

### If you exclude tests

31 of those 38 sites are in-package tests, so production-only fan-in for `CompileToStatement` drops to 7. On that basis the leader is:

**`(*renderer).addArg` — `internal/filter/render.go:842` — 28 call sites from 14 distinct methods**, all within `render.go` (`renderScalarComparison`, `renderTagEquals`, `renderRegex`, `foldedLike`, etc.). It's the placeholder-binding helper every SQL fragment funnels through.

Runners-up under `internal/` (non-test call sites): `filter.Field` ~19, `email.NewClient` ~18, `filter.jsonArrayExpr` ~16, `util.GenUUID` ~7 non-test / 28 total.

### One caveat on the raw graph numbers

The knowledge-graph index reports much higher counts for `internal/version.Len` (179), `internal/scheduler.Error` (142), and `internal/scheduler.Next` (42) — these are name-collision artifacts, not real fan-in. I checked the call sites: they're `require.Len(t, …)`/`require.Error(t, …)` from testify, `err.Error()`, `bytes.Buffer.Len()`, and `sql.Rows.Next()` in `store/db/*`, mis-attributed to the same-named `SortVersion.Len` (`internal/version/version.go:44`), `slogAdapter.Error` (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:89`, a test-only type), and the cron `Next`. `SortVersion` is referenced in exactly two places in the whole repo.
